core_obligations: Construct the integral cover (proof lines 14481-14487): write X = Spec(A) with A = Z[x_i]/J, let R be the integral closure of Z[x_i] in an algebraic closure of its fraction field, and put A' = R/JR and X' = Spec(A'); the vanishing lemma over absolutely algebraically closed rings gives assertion (1) for every closed subscheme of X'.

Reduce a class to a finite level (proof lines 14489-14498): for a class xi on a closed subscheme Z of X, the cover X' -> X is integral and surjective, so xi dies on X' x_X Z; writing X' as a filtered limit of schemes X'_i finite and of finite presentation over X (the affine case being the special case of the Limits lemma), the directed colimit description of cohomology shows that xi already dies on X'_i x_X Z for some i, which is assertion (2).
proof_roadmap: Realise X as a quotient of a polynomial ring and take the integral closure of the polynomial ring in an algebraic closure of its fraction field.
Use the vanishing lemma over absolutely algebraically closed rings to get the integral cover of part (1).
For part (2), present the integral cover as a filtered limit of finite finitely presented covers and use the colimit description of cohomology to descend the vanishing to a finite level.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for an affine scheme, an integral cover on which all higher cohomology of finite constant coefficients vanishes, and shows that any given class is already killed by a finite finitely presented cover (statement lines 14466-14478). The proof (proof lines 14480-14498) builds the cover from the integral closure of a polynomial ring inside an algebraic closure of its fraction field, applies the vanishing lemma over absolutely algebraically closed rings, and then descends the vanishing of a prescribed class to a finite level using the presentation of the integral morphism as a filtered limit and the colimit description of cohomology. H2: one construction plus one limit descent, written out.
